description: Go MCP server for GitLab: 2 dynamic tools reach 1000+ REST/GraphQL actions. Free/CE, no paid tier.

tool_signatures.name: Format for this project
tool_signatures.description: catalog action IDs are {domain}.{action} (issue.create, project.list); on the individual surface the declared name is domain-first, gitlab_{domain}_{action} (gitlab_issue_create, gitlab_project_list), with a legacy verb-first set (gitlab_list_issue_discussions) that stays as declared. New actions take the domain-first form; the name is IndividualTool.Name in the ActionSpec, never derived by formula. Meta-tools are the bare domain (gitlab_issue) with the operation in the action argument

tool_signatures.name: The action segment is a verb
tool_signatures.description: get, list, search, create, update, delete

tool_signatures.name: Be specific
tool_signatures.description: Avoid generic names that could conflict with other servers

tool_signatures.name: Descriptions
tool_signatures.description: Must narrowly and unambiguously describe functionality, matching actual behavior

tool_signatures.name: Annotation
tool_signatures.description: Type

tool_signatures.description: ReadOnlyHint=true, DestructiveHint=false, IdempotentHint=true

tool_signatures.name: Tag fields that only exist at a higher GitLab tier with tier
tool_signatures.description: "premium" or tier:"ultimate"; the catalog prunes them from the schema below that tier

tool_signatures.name: Use jsonschema
tool_signatures.description: "description,required" for a field GitLab requires on the route the action sends, and only for that: the marker is the one required list all three surfaces serve (omitempty no longer decides it), and make audit-1to1-required fails on a marker the live record disagrees with unless cmd/audit_1to1/internal/required/declarations.go says why. A choice between fields GitLab states as at_least_one_of is an anyOf through toolutil.SchemaAnyOfRequired in the spec's InputSchemaOverrides, and one it states as exactly_one_of a oneOf through toolutil.SchemaOneOfRequired, with neither field marked; only the SDK's schema validation holds a call to one oneOf branch, so the handler of an exactly_one_of also refuses a call naming two of the fields before it sends anything, as groupldap's do. A rule on each element of a list is an items override on that list (toolutil.SchemaItemsOneOfRequired, SchemaItemsAnyOfRequired, SchemaItemsAnyOfRequiredUnlessTrue and SchemaItemsAtMostOneOf, built on toolutil.SchemaItemsOverride), and since neither the meta nor the dynamic dispatcher reads an item schema, the handler refuses an element that breaks it, as the protected environment protect and update do through toolutil.CheckEnvironmentProtect and CheckEnvironmentUpdate

tool_signatures.name: Use json
tool_signatures.description: ",omitempty" for optional fields

tool_signatures.name: A membership access level parameter publishes the levels its route accepts and no other, from toolutil.AccessLevelSet in internal/toolutil/access_level.go (ProjectAccessLevels, GroupAccessLevels and the rest, read from GitLab's routes and models)
tool_signatures.description: SchemaOverride (or SchemaItemsOverride for a list) in the spec's InputSchemaOverrides makes it an integer enum, and its jsonschema description lists the same levels as N=Role. min_access_level and shared_min_access_level get theirs centrally. TestBuildActionCatalog_MembershipAccessLevels_OfferOnlyWhatTheRouteAccepts in internal/tools fails on such a parameter it does not map to a set, and on a description that offers a level outside it

tool_signatures.name: A string whose form GitLab checks publishes that form, so a model knows what to send and find's example fills it with a value of it rather than "value"
tool_signatures.description: a format through toolutil.SchemaFormatOverride (dates, URLs and email get theirs centrally, on a plain string only, so a nullable or nested one is overridden per action), or a pattern through toolutil.SchemaPatternOverride, with toolutil.CronPattern for a cron expression and toolutil.FullCommitSHAPattern for a SHA where GitLab holds the parameter to a full one. A SHA that also takes a ref name, a duration, and a field cleared with an empty string get no pattern, since it would refuse values GitLab takes, and a string that takes several values in one, an invitation's comma-separated emails or an OAuth application's redirect URIs one per line, gets no format, since a format names one value: toolutil.SchemaNoFormatOverride keeps a central one off it. TestFind_FormatBearingParams_DeclareTheirFormatAndExampleIt in internal/tools/dynamic holds every required parameter of the catalog to it

tool_signatures.name: NotFoundResult(resource, identifier, hints...) — in get handlers on IsHTTPStatus(err, 404)
tool_signatures.description: an informational IsError result logged at INFO, with nil error

tool_signatures.name: IsPermissionRefusal(err) + WrapErrWithHint
tool_signatures.description: for a hint that names a role, a license or an owner. GitLab refuses a missing permission with 401 at many routes, so do not scope such a hint to 403, and do not key it on 401 alone, which also matches a token GitLab rejected

tool_signatures.name: Pick the constructor that matches the operation
tool_signatures.description: NewReadActionSpec, NewCreateActionSpec, NewUpdateActionSpec, NewAdditiveActionSpec, or NewDeleteActionSpec; each presets ReadOnly, Destructive, and Idempotent. A destructive action's route must be built with toolutil.DestructiveAction (returns an output) or toolutil.DestructiveVoidAction (returns only an error), which gate execution behind confirmation.

tool_signatures.name: Set Edition (free / premium / ultimate; empty means free) on each spec. In internal/tools/action_catalog.go, filterActionSpecGroupsByTier withholds an action whose edition exceeds the tier resolved from GITLAB_MCP_TIER / --tier, and pruneSchemaFieldsByTier removes the tier
tool_signatures.description: "..."-tagged fields from the schemas.

tool_signatures.name: A hint names an action by its canonical ID, through toolutil.HintAction(id, purpose) or the ID itself, never by a gitlab_ tool name, and so does every other sentence a model reads
tool_signatures.description: an error's message, a refusal, a Usage line, parameter guidance and a field's description, in a jsonschema tag or a schema override map. A tool name is right on one surface of three, and make check-action-ids fails on it. A bare meta action name (Use action 'list') resolves on the meta surface alone and no gate reads it, so write toolutil.HintAction("package.list", ...) instead

tool_signatures.name: Empty state
tool_signatures.description: always handle len(items) == 0

tool_signatures.name: A case table (for _, tt
tool_signatures.description: = range tests) must run each case under t.Run (make check-test-subtests; go run ./cmd/audit_test_subtests/ -fix rewrites the unambiguous shapes)

tool_signatures.name: Never t.Fatal/t.Fatalf/t.FailNow inside an httptest handler or any other goroutine
tool_signatures.description: t.Errorf + a deterministic response + return, or record with atomics and assert afterwards (.github/instructions/test-goroutines.instructions.md; make check-test-goroutines). testutil.AssertRequestPath / AssertRequestMethod / AssertQueryParam and testutil.ForbiddenHandler already follow the contract

tool_signatures.name: [ ] Documentation updated
tool_signatures.description: the tool reference regenerated (make gen-tool-reference), the site's counts refreshed (make gen-site-stats), and any hand-written site page the action changes edited in English and Spanish
